title: serving-runtime daily scratchpad - 2026-03-17
content:
Daily scratchpad - quick notes + triage (personal)
Date: 2026-03-17
Owner: Maya Chen (eng-serving-runtime)

Top priorities
- unblock customer A (high qps) by EOD: fallback routing not triggering for model-variant mismatch (SERV-4921).
- repro slow tail-latency on rn-large with kv-cache warmup: need perf harness run for sequence lengths 256/512.
- land small kernel patch that avoids memcpy on kv-cache eviction (PR #1283) - still failing CI on ampere-2 + cuda 12.2.

Triage notes
1) SERV-4921: fallback routing ignoring pinning
   - symptoms: when primary variant oom'd, requests get queued instead of routed to cheaper-quantized variant.
   - first-pass: config check shows routing-policy set to fallback:true. Logs show "route_decision: STICKY" near time of incident.
   - hypothesis: sticky routing cookie isn't expiring on capacity fail leading to sticky to same instance. Possible bug in cookie invalidation when fallback triggered.
   - next: add extra log around RoutePolicy::evaluate -> write minimal repro with envoy proxy simulate capacity signal. Assign Jon.

2) PR #1283 (kv-cache eviction memcpy optimization)
   - goal: eliminate memcpy on eviction path to reduce p99 CPU and copies when cache churn high.
   - CI failures on Ampere-2 + CUDA12.2: segfault in cuMemFree path after patch. Local repro on dev machine shows double-free when eviction race occurs.
   - suspect: race between eviction thread and refill path - missing atomic flag around buffer ownership.
   - quick fix: add a CAS ownership flag and skip free if not owner. Test locally with stressed evict/refill harness.
   - follow-up: add sanitizer/asan-ish run in CI for GPU mem issues (costly but worth for kernel changes).

3) tail-latency regressions on rn-large (reported by infra-alert)
   - observed: p99 increased from 140ms -> 260ms after latest kernel scheduler tweak (2026-03-10). Affected sequences >256.
   - initial profiling: CPU scheduling spikes while kernel launches queue up, NVLink transfer times increased slightly.
   - experiments to run:
     * run per-kernel timing with perfkit across seq lengths 128/256/512.
     * try batching cap at 16 vs 32 to see latency vs throughput curve.
     * enable continuous batching backpressure limiter to avoid huge batches for long seqs.
   - assign Eleni to run perfkit and upload flamegraphs to the linked PR.

Small TODOs / reminders
- Add note to rollout playbook for automatic fallback: include metric that shows "fallback_count" and add PagerDuty rule if fallback > 5% for 5m.
- Follow up with product on acceptable cost/latency tradeoff for quantized variant for customer A.
- Add test case to e2e suite: simulate primary OOM -> verify routing to secondary variant within 500ms.
- Clean up logging noise: remove debug log in Router::decide emitted every request (was left in from earlier debugging).
- Measure mem footprint of kv-cache entries after quantization: need script to sample entry sizes across models.

Kernel notes / ideas
- Experiment: do not memcpy on kv-cache eviction; instead use double-buffering and swap pointers under lock. Avoid frees on hot path.
- Consider per-thread allocator for small token buffers to reduce contention.
- Revisit attention kernel: try alternative fused attention for seq < 128 and tiled attention for >128; benchmark tradeoffs.
- Quantized matmul: maybe use int8 GEMM path for ffwrd dense when batch_size > 8 - measure model quality impact.

Logs / commands to run (quick)
- reproduce kv-cache race locally:
  ./tools/stress-kv-cache --model rn-large --threads 24 --seq 512 --duration 120s
- perfkit runs:
  ./perfkit/run.sh --model rn-large --seqs 128,256,512 --batch-caps 8,16,32 --out /tmp/perf-2026-03-17
- repro fallback routing:
  tools/simulate-capacity-change --target-instance id=svc-02 --cpu 95 --duration 30s --observe router-logs

Open questions / blockers
- Is it acceptable to add GPU mem sanitizer in CI (time/cost)? propose enabling on main branch weekly rather than per-PR.
- For fallback routing bug: are there other stateful cookies (session affinity) that can cause sticky decisions? Need product input.

Notes to self
- keep changes minimal for next stable release (small lock + CAS) to fix double-free; plan proper rewrite in next sprint.
- Document the eviction ownership model in code comments and confluence page.

References
- PR #1283: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1283
- Ticket: SERV-4921 (fallback routing)
- Confluence: serving-runtime-kernel-opts

End of scratchpad
